newsitem.title: USA: AT&T again seeks state arbitration.
newsitem.headline: AT&T again seeks state arbitration.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Monday it asked the Louisiana Public Service Commission to arbitrate its negotiations with BellSouth Corp.

Following passage of the federal law allowing local competition, AT&T notified local exchange carriers in all 50 states that it wanted to launch negotiations. AT&T has since requested arbitration in four other states in the Southeast: North Carolina, Florida, Georgia and Tennessee.
Formal talks began in Lousiana April 15th, AT&T said.

While some issues have been worked out, AT&T said, major issues remaining are: what services AT&T would buy from BellSouth and then resell to customers; transfer of customer records, information and other customer-service issues, including branding, operator services and directory assistance hand-offs; operational details; to what degree BellSouth would unbundle its network; and the prices of unbundled network elements and interconnection as well as the prices for resold services.

AT&T said because the Louisiana commission has been very progressive in its handling of resale and interconnection, AT&T delayed its filing to give the commission more time to consider these specific issues.

"While the issues surrounding local telephone competition are currently under consideration by the commission, it was necessary for AT&T to protect its options under the federal act by filing for arbitration," AT&T explained.
